locator: Middle Ages / Europe and Vikings; Early modern; Modern

variants.en: All medieval European scholars believed Earth was flat.
variants.zh: 所有中世纪欧洲学者都相信地球是平的。

correction.en: A spherical Earth was well known among medieval European scholars.
correction.zh: 球形地球在中世纪欧洲学者中已广为人知。

variants.en: Columbus was the first European ever to reach the Americas.
variants.zh: 哥伦布是最早到达美洲的欧洲人。

correction.en: Norse travelers reached North America centuries earlier.
correction.zh: 北欧旅行者早数百年就到达了北美。

variants.en: Columbus's voyage first established that Earth is round to European scholars.
variants.zh: 哥伦布的航行首次向欧洲学者证明地球是圆的。

correction.en: Scholars already knew the spherical shape; debate concerned travel distance.
correction.zh: 学者早已知道球形；争论涉及航行距离。

variants.en: Horned helmets were the standard headgear of Viking warriors.
variants.zh: 带角头盔是维京武士的标准头具。

correction.en: There is no evidence supporting horned helmets as standard Viking warrior equipment.
correction.zh: 没有证据支持带角头盔是维京武士的标准装备。

variants.en: Medieval Europeans universally avoided bathing throughout the Middle Ages.
variants.zh: 中世纪欧洲人在整个时期都不洗澡。

correction.en: Bathing and public bathhouses existed in medieval Europe.
correction.zh: 中世纪欧洲存在洗澡习俗和公共浴室。

variants.en: Historical records prove that an apple struck Newton's head and immediately created his gravity theory.
variants.zh: 历史记录证明苹果砸中牛顿的头并立即造成引力理论。

correction.en: Accounts describe observing a falling apple, not verified impact on his head or instant theory creation.
correction.zh: 记载描述了观察落下的苹果，而非已证实的头部撞击或瞬间创造理论。

variants.en: Albert Einstein failed his mathematics classes at school.
variants.zh: 爱因斯坦在学校的数学课不及格。

correction.en: Einstein excelled in mathematics; his early entrance-exam difficulties concerned other subjects.
correction.zh: 爱因斯坦擅长数学；早期入学考试的困难涉及其他科目。

variants.en: Napoleon was exceptionally short compared with typical French men of his era.
variants.zh: 拿破仑比同时代普通法国男性特别矮。

correction.en: His recorded height is near the era's male average; French and English units differ.
correction.zh: 他的记录身高接近当时男性平均值；法国和英国单位不同。

variants.en: Plymouth Pilgrims normally wore only black clothes and buckled hats.
variants.zh: 普利茅斯朝圣者通常只穿黑衣和带扣帽子。

correction.en: Their everyday clothing included colors; the stereotyped buckled hats are later imagery.
correction.zh: 他们的日常衣服有多种颜色；带扣帽子是后来的刻板形象。

variants.en: Roman soldiers received their regular wages as bags of salt instead of money.
variants.zh: 罗马士兵的日常工资是一袋袋盐而不是货币。

correction.en: The salary/salt etymology does not establish that regular wages were paid in salt.
correction.zh: 工资与盐的词源关联不能证明常规工资用盐支付。

variants.en: Michelangelo painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling while lying flat on his back.
variants.zh: 米开朗基罗平躺着绘制了西斯廷教堂天花板。

correction.en: He worked standing on scaffolding rather than lying flat.
correction.zh: 他站在脚手架上工作，而不是平躺。

variants.en: Ancient Greek and Roman marble statues were always left unpainted white.
variants.zh: 古希腊和罗马的大理石雕像始终保持未上色的白色。

correction.en: Many classical statues originally bore painted colors that have deteriorated.
correction.zh: 许多古典雕像原有彩绘，颜料后来退化。
